titulo: Biosphere 2: o experimento no deserto do Arizona (Albert Einstein 2026)
texto_base:
In the middle of the vast Arizona desert, in the United States, there's a structure that seems taken straight out of the pages of science fiction. Inside a massive complex of glass pyramids and towers, spread across 1.2 hectares, stands a tropical rainforest topped by a 7.6-meter-high waterfall, a savannah and a fog desert. It's seemingly a little capsule of Earth, which is why the structure is called Biosphere 2 — named after our own planet, Biosphere 1.

The scenery forms the perfect background for the futuristic experiment that once took place here. In the early 1990s, eight people locked themselves inside, sealed off from the outside world for two years, to explore the challenges of living in a self-contained system — a prerequisite for building colonies in outer space. They fed themselves from the crops they grew, they recycled their own wastewater and they cared for the plants that produced their oxygen.

In terms of sustaining human life, the experiment did not go well. Oxygen levels fell significantly, making the inhabitants sick, while carbon dioxide (CO2) levels increased. Countless animals died, including the pollinators the plants needed to reproduce. And although the "biospherians" did survive on their homegrown food, they lost weight to the point where they became a case study for calorie restriction. When supplementary oxygen needed to be brought in, commentators blamed the project as a failure, calling it a "new-age silliness masquerading as science". In recent years, however, many experts have come to see the Biosphere 2 experiment in a new light, with valuable lessons about ecology, atmospheric science and importantly, the irreplaceability of our own planet.

(Katarina Zimmer. www.bbc.com, 05.07.2025. Adapted.)
alternativas: the Biosphere 2 experiment, with its weaknesses and lessons to be learned.
controversies between experts about the value of the Biosphere 2 project.
the dangers of trying to artificially reproduce Earth's environment and life.
the efforts of the research team to survive inside the Biosphere 2 facility.
the Biosphere 2 structure, with its glass buildings and wide surroundings.
comentario: A questão pede a ideia central, e o texto percorre o experimento inteiro: descreve a estrutura, conta o que deu errado ("the experiment did not go well") e fecha com o aprendizado ("valuable lessons about ecology, atmospheric science and importantly, the irreplaceability of our own planet"). As falhas e as lições são justamente os dois eixos da alternativa A. A alternativa E fica só no primeiro parágrafo, que é cenário, e a D isola a sobrevivência da equipe, que é um detalhe. A B inverte o texto: não há controvérsia entre especialistas, e sim uma reavaliação posterior favorável ao projeto.
meta_description: Questão de inglês do vestibular Albert Einstein 2026 sobre o experimento Biosphere 2, com gabarito comentado em português.

titulo: A little capsule of Earth: sentido da expressão (Albert Einstein 2026)
texto_base:
In the middle of the vast Arizona desert, in the United States, there's a structure that seems taken straight out of the pages of science fiction. Inside a massive complex of glass pyramids and towers, spread across 1.2 hectares, stands a tropical rainforest topped by a 7.6-meter-high waterfall, a savannah and a fog desert. It's seemingly a little capsule of Earth, which is why the structure is called Biosphere 2 — named after our own planet, Biosphere 1.

(Katarina Zimmer. www.bbc.com, 05.07.2025. Adapted.)
enunciado: In the fragment from the first paragraph "It's seemingly a little capsule of Earth", the underlined expression means
alternativas: a miniature of Earth.
a geological formation on Earth's surface.
a portion of Earth inside a capsule.
a remedy capsule to save the Earth.
a spaceship capsule down on Earth.
comentario: A expressão aparece logo depois da lista de ambientes reunidos num só lugar — floresta tropical, savana e deserto — e é justificada pela frase seguinte, que explica o nome Biosphere 2 "named after our own planet, Biosphere 1". Trata-se, portanto, de uma reprodução da Terra em escala reduzida: uma miniatura. As alternativas D e E tomam "capsule" no sentido literal de cápsula de remédio ou de nave, sentidos que o contexto não sustenta.

titulo: The scenery: a que se refere o termo (Albert Einstein 2026)
texto_base:
In the middle of the vast Arizona desert, in the United States, there's a structure that seems taken straight out of the pages of science fiction. Inside a massive complex of glass pyramids and towers, spread across 1.2 hectares, stands a tropical rainforest topped by a 7.6-meter-high waterfall, a savannah and a fog desert. It's seemingly a little capsule of Earth, which is why the structure is called Biosphere 2 — named after our own planet, Biosphere 1.

The scenery forms the perfect background for the futuristic experiment that once took place here. In the early 1990s, eight people locked themselves inside, sealed off from the outside world for two years, to explore the challenges of living in a self-contained system.

(Katarina Zimmer. www.bbc.com, 05.07.2025. Adapted.)
enunciado: In the excerpt from the second paragraph "The scenery forms the perfect background for the futuristic experiment that once took place here", the underlined term refers to
alternativas: the perfectness with which Biosphere 2 was constructed.
the desert of Arizona and its geographical features.
the innovative architecture of the Biosphere 2 complex.
the unusual experience of living inside a capsule for two years.
the science fiction reality of the Biosphere 2 human colony.
comentario: "The scenery" abre o segundo parágrafo retomando o que acabou de ser descrito no primeiro: "a massive complex of glass pyramids and towers" com floresta, savana e deserto dentro. É o conjunto arquitetônico de Biosphere 2, e não a paisagem natural do Arizona, que serve apenas para localizar a estrutura — o que elimina a alternativa B. A D e a E falam do experimento e de sua atmosfera, mas o termo retoma o cenário físico, não a experiência vivida.
meta_description: Questão de referência textual do vestibular Albert Einstein 2026 sobre o termo the scenery, com gabarito comentado em português.

titulo: O desequilíbrio ecológico dentro do Biosphere 2 (Albert Einstein 2026)
texto_base:
In terms of sustaining human life, the experiment did not go well. Oxygen levels fell significantly, making the inhabitants sick, while carbon dioxide (CO2) levels increased. Countless animals died, including the pollinators the plants needed to reproduce. And although the "biospherians" did survive on their homegrown food, they lost weight to the point where they became a case study for calorie restriction. When supplementary oxygen needed to be brought in, commentators blamed the project as a failure, calling it a "new-age silliness masquerading as science".

(Katarina Zimmer. www.bbc.com, 05.07.2025. Adapted.)
enunciado: According to the third paragraph, one major ecological imbalance that compromised human habitability in Biosphere 2 was the
alternativas: unexpected incident leading to illnesses and death.
severe food diet program the research team were forced to.
oscillation of oxygen levels inside the capsule.
extermination of a number of animal species and plants.
impact of expanded carbon dioxide levels.
comentario: O parágrafo aponta duas mudanças simultâneas na atmosfera: "Oxygen levels fell significantly, making the inhabitants sick, while carbon dioxide (CO2) levels increased". A alternativa E capta o aumento do gás carbônico, que é o desequilíbrio ecológico descrito. A alternativa C erra ao falar em "oscillation": o texto diz que o oxigênio caiu, não que oscilou. A B trata da perda de peso, que foi consequência da alimentação e não um desequilíbrio ecológico, e a D fala em extermínio de plantas, que o texto não afirma.
meta_description: Questão do vestibular Albert Einstein 2026 sobre o desequilíbrio ecológico no Biosphere 2, com gabarito comentado em português.
